: O R D E R :
HONBLE
JUSTICE SRI KALIDAS MUKHERJEE, PRESIDENT 

 

 

 

 This
appeal is directed against the judgment and order passed by Learned District
Forum, Kolkata, Unit-I in case no.111 of 2008 allowing the complaint against OP
Nos.1 and 2 with cost and dismissing the case against OP No.3. The Learned District Forum has directed the
OP Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally to refund the ticket money of Rs.6,574/-;
to pay Rs.15,000/- as compensation and Rs.7,000/- as litigation cost within 45
days from the date of communication of the order, in default the interest @ 9%
p.a. shall accrue over the entire amount till realization.
The
case of the complainant/respondent, in short, is that he was traveling to Bermuda at the place of his job and, as such, purchased
one e-ticket from Mercury Travels Ltd., Kolkata for the flight. The complainant on reaching Mumbai by
connecting flight IC 0273 at 18.30 hrs. on 13/06/07 wanted to avail the next
flight from Mumbai BA 0138 at 2.15 hrs. on 14/06/07 for his onward journey to London and Bermuda. The said IC 0273 on 13/06/07 was delayed due
to strike called by the Indian Airlines ground staff and, as such, the
complainant had to travel by another airline after purchasing a fresh ticket
from Kolkata to Mumbai by Indigo 6E 322 dated 13/06/07, the cost of which was
Rs.6,574/-. The Indian Airlines Duty
Manager said the money was completely refundable or the flight to be endorsed
to another airlines for all the passengers.
But as the Indian Airlines did not give any endorsed slip to the
complainant, a fresh ticket had to be purchased by another airline. The complainants father followed up the
matter in his absence, but he did not get any positive response from Mercury
Travels Ltd., British Airways and Indian Airlines. The complainant had to come back to Kolkata
from Bermuda to follow up the matter. The Mercury Travels Ltd. advised him to
follow up the matter with British Airways office in Kolkata and Indian
Airlines. The complainant talked to British
Airways office in Kolkata, but they said Please note that there is no refund
since the sector CCU-BOM forms a part of the through fare CCU-BDA-CCU and if
the Indian Airlines flight was delayed that was not due to any fault on the
part of British Airways. Indian Airlines
on being approached by the complainant told that as it was a free ticket they
could not refund or endorse the same to any other airlines. It was further told that the document was
issued by British Airways and the complainant ought to have taken up the matter
with British Airways. For the said reason,
the complaint was filed before the Learned District Forum.
The
Learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that there was a strike called
by the staff of the Indian Airlines on 13/06/07 and, as such, the complainant
had to purchase a ticket by Indigo flight.
It is contended that there is no dispute as to the travel from Mumbai to
Bermuda and therefrom to London and back, but the dispute relates to the flight
by Indian Airlines from Kolkata to Mumbai for which the OP No.3 of the
complaint, that is, Indian Airlines is responsible. It is submitted that British Airways is not
concerned at all with the dispute and the Learned District Forum wrongly held
the appellant responsible for the deficiency in service and passed the impugned
order. It is submitted that there was no
fault on the part of the British Airways.
It
is submitted by the respondent no.1/complainant that the complainant had to
face troubles as the flight of Indian Airlines was cancelled due to strike called
by the staff of the said airlines and under such circumstances, he had to purchase ticket of another
airlines. It is submitted that the
Indian Airlines did neither arrange for the flight with any other airlines nor
did refund the amount of the ticket.
It
is submitted by the Learned Counsel for the respondent no.2 (travel agency)
that there was no deficiency in service by the travel agency.
It
has been submitted by the respondent no.3/Indian Airlines that it was a
circumstance beyond control and, as such, there was no deficiency in service on
the part of Indian Airlines. The Learned
Counsel has referred to the decision reported in
IV (2005) CPJ 186 (NC)
[Beechins Creation Pvt. Ltd. Vs. T.M.A. International Airlines
].
We
have heard the submission made by both sides and perused the papers on
record. Evidently, the dispute relates
to the flight by Indian Airlines on 13/06/07 from Kolkata to Mumbai. Admittedly, there was a strike called by the
staff of the Indian Airlines for which the said flight was cancelled. The Indian Airlines filed W.V. before the
Learned District Forum wherein at Para 7 it has been averred that as per normal
practice in case of disruption of flights, the tickets of the passengers either
are refunded in full or endorsed to other airlines subject to availability of
seats and agreement for endorsement, but the facts and circumstances of the
instant case were different and for that reason the normal practice would not
be applicable for the complainant. It
is, therefore, an admitted fact that there was provision for either refund of
the amount of ticket or endorsement of the ticket to any other airlines. It is the specific contention of the
respondent no.3 that due to strike called by the staff of the Indian Airlines,
no such arrangement or refund could be made.
In this connection the respondent no.3 has relied on the aforesaid
decision. We are of the considered view
that
the said decision
relates to carriage of goods and there was delay due to
strike of the airport ground staff and the consignment was accepted without any
demur. But the facts of the instant case
are different because of the fact that the complainant after reaching Mumbai by
the said flight of Indian Airlines was to avail the next flight of British
Airways for his journey from Mumbai to Bermuda and London.
Under such circumstances, we are of the view that the aforesaid decision
of the Hon'ble National Commission is not applicable in the circumstances of
the instant case. There was deficiency
on the part of the Indian Airlines, that is, respondent no.3 herein for which
the respondent no.3 only is liable to refund the amount of purchase of the
ticket, compensation and litigation cost.
There was no fault on the part of appellant British Airways and the
respondent no.2 Mercury Travels Ltd. The
impugned judgment is, therefore, modified as hereunder.
The
appeal is allowed in part. The
respondent no.3 is directed to refund the amount of the ticket to the tune of
Rs.6,574/-; pay the compensation of Rs.12,000/- and litigation cost of Rs.5,000/-
to the complainant/respondent within 45 days from this date failing which an
interest @ 9% p.a. shall accrue on the entire amount till realization. The impugned judgment stands modified to the
extent stated above.
MEMBER(L) PRESIDENT
